To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Cry toxins are pore-forming toxins that insert into the midgut of insects and kill them by forming pores in their midgut epithelium; Cyt toxins also insert into membranes and kill by a similar mechanism.

(i) the mode of action and the phylogeny of Cry and Cty toxins are very similar; (ii) Cry and Cyt synergize each other's toxicity and (iii) Cry and Cty are potential candidates for the development of new insecticides.
the Cry and Cyt proteins are a diverse group with activity against a broad range of insects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of action of Cry toxins and their interaction with receptors and the host membrane.

understanding the molecular basis of Cry and Cty toxin activity and how they can be used to develop more effective bioinsecticides for controlling agricultural insect pests, insect vectors and for the development of transgenic crops.
the development of novel insecticidal proteins that can be used to control insect pests and vectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mode of action and the diversity of Cry and Cty toxins are a result of their evolution as insecticidal agents.
Cry proteins kill insects by binding to specific receptors, and Cyt toxins kill insects by directly interacting with the membrane lipids.

the mechanism of action of these insecticidal toxins has been established in a few insect species and in a few cases in mammalian cells, but that there is a long way to go before a comprehensive understanding of their mode of action in all target insects is achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cry toxins are a diverse group with a common mechanism of action that can be used in the control of a wide range of insect pests.
Cry toxins are a group of proteins with high specificity for insects, and are a promising alternative for insect pest control.
Cry and Cyt proteins are a diverse group that evolved by different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cry toxins are highly specific and that their mode of action can be overcome by the evolution of resistance.
the 3-domain Cry toxins are the only PFT that are used for insect control and their mode of insecticidal action is different from that of other PFT that are toxic to mammals.
the mode of action and diversity of the 1-Domain Cyt toxins is similar to that of the 3-domain Cry family, and that the Cyt proteins may play a role in overcoming resistance to Cry toxins.
